**Best fit: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its **2,600 W AC output** is enough for a typical single-burner induction cooktop (up to about **1,800 W**) and most electric kettles; its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives it useful capacity for cooking or repeated boils. Check your appliance’s label to make sure its wattage is below the station’s continuous output. ([Specs and product details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

For a cooktop, expect roughly **an hour of continuous high-power use** from a 2,000 Wh-class station; simmering and ordinary meal prep use less. A kettle is a shorter load: the cited guide estimates about **90–110 Wh to boil one litre**. ([Runtime guidance](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop), [kettle estimate and station comparison](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))
